conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice; D is bounded and Lebesgue measurable with 0 < M = |D| < infinity, k > 0, and contrasts are complex L-infinity classes extended by zero outside D.
The outgoing kernel is exp(ik|z|)/(4π|z|), assigned zero at z = 0; the volume equation is u = f + K(q)u. The exact scattering family is defined only when ||K(q)|| < 1.
The Fourier transform uses exp(-2πi y·ξ); the Born sample is the zero-extended contrast's Fourier value at k(θ-d)/(2π), divided by 4π.

Fréchet differentiability is asserted at zero for each fixed direction pair, with complex parameter and scalar spaces viewed as real Banach spaces; the remainder estimate is uniform over direction pairs.

Finite coefficient inner products are linear in the first argument. Reduced SVD sums include only positive singular values; the zero matrix uses an empty sum. Budget zero returns no estimate; every positive budget permits exactly one filter application. Discrepancy status includes equality R = δ.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the small-norm contrast class by ρ_k(q) = ||K(q)|| < 1, the unique volume solution, the exact outgoing far-field family, and the first Born family with Fourier frequency k(θ-d)/(2π).

The small-norm contrast class is open and contains zero. On that class the volume solution exists uniquely, the exact and Born integrals converge absolutely and are representative-independent, and the exact data are continuous in observation direction and satisfy the stated uniform outgoing far-field estimate.

Uniformly over incident and observation directions, the exact-minus-Born error is at most M||q||∞ρ/(4π(1-ρ)); when C_D||q||∞ < 1 it is at most MC_D||q||∞²/(4π(1-C_D||q||∞)). For each fixed direction pair the real Fréchet derivative at zero is the Born functional.

Defines the finite cell-integral Born matrix, a reduced-SVD filtered estimate, the zero-budget branch, and one-pass reconstruction and residual-status outputs for positive budgets. It asserts no nonlinear recovery or infinite-dimensional exact-range test.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite defines identifiability through equality of exact data and treats stability separately. The assigned page imports no uniqueness or stability theorem. Its finite-sample example constructs distinct contrasts with identical Born samples and explicitly limits the conclusion to the finite linearized model.

The algorithm's Picard reference preserves both requirements for exact range membership: orthogonality to the adjoint kernel and finiteness of the Picard sum. The supplier separately characterizes the pseudoinverse domain without the orthogonality requirement. The algorithm correctly uses the result only to explain why its finite residual is not an infinite-dimensional exact-range test.
